Definition: to dispart (the feet or lips), i.e. become licentious
BiblicalUsage: Pasaq means to dispart, to open wide, to become licentious. Ezekiel says in Ezekiel 16:25 that Jerusalem opened her feet to every one that passed by, multiplying her whoredoms. Proverbs 13:3 warns that he that openeth wide his lips shall have destruction.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that an open mouth and an open life go together in these verses, and the lips that are not guarded will destroy the one who opens them.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
